faq.q: How do I make a picture in my head?
faq.a: Read a sentence, then stop and close your eyes. Think: what would this look like? Think about the colours, the people and the place.
Think about who is there, where they are, the colours and the sounds. More details make your picture clearer.
Change your picture to match the story. Good readers keep changing their picture as they read.
asks: What happens when the story changes?

faq.q: Why does picturing help me read?
faq.a: Making a picture helps you understand what is happening. It also helps you remember it later.

faq.q: What if I cannot make a picture in my head?
faq.a: That is okay, every mind works differently. You can draw a quick picture on paper instead, or talk about what is happening with a grown-up.
asks: I cannot see pictures in my head

facts: Making pictures in your mind while you read is called visualising.
Many reading teachers teach visualising as a way to understand and remember stories.

quiz.say: The kite flies away. What does Ama do with her picture?
quiz.show: 🪁 The kite flies away. What does Ama do?
quiz.why: Ama changes her picture so it matches the new part of the story.

wrong.0: The old picture shows the kite in the sky, but now it has flown away.
wrong.2: Ama can change her picture and keep reading.

quiz.say: Which detail belongs in your picture of the story?
quiz.show: Which detail belongs in your story picture?
quiz.why: The colour of the kite comes from the story. It helps your picture match the words.

wrong.0: Your lunch is a different thing, outside this story.
wrong.1: Your favourite number is outside this story.
